judged_text: The credential-sync branch does not send the refresh token or any per-app OAuth context (only calcomUserId and appSlug) to the sync endpoint, so the contract relies entirely on the parent application holding the actual OAuth client secret and refresh token — yet the webhook handler in this same PR persists key objects created from this flow. Two hand-maintained halves of a protocol (the sync fetch body and the app-credential webhook payload) evolve independently with no shared schema; a self-hoster implementing the documented endpoint must guess the response shape, and any mismatch is only discovered as runtime failures in provider-specific code paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the sync endpoint call in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` (no refresh token or other OAuth context), explicitly relying on the external application to manage secrets/tokens. Separately, the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` persists decrypted `keys` into `prisma.credential`, and the runtime parsing behavior changes via `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (switching to a minimal schema when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set). There is no shared/request/response schema tying the sync endpoint contract to the webhook payload contract, so mismatches would surface only at runtime in provider-specific refresh flows—this is a concrete protocol/architecture concern grounded in the added code, but not a directly provable functional defect from the diff alone.
